title.en: Empathy, life skills, and constitutional values

text.en: Health is not just physical fitness—it includes how we listen, forgive, respect equality, and build warm relationships. Social health turns a group of individuals into a caring society.

WHO defines health as complete physical, mental, emotional, and social well-being. Social health means interacting positively and harmoniously with family, peers, and society.
Socially healthy people listen respectfully, practise equality (like Arun insisting a poor boy not be pushed to the back of a food queue), admit mistakes, and reconnect with old friends.
Our Constitution's ideals—Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity—guide fair and considerate social behaviour.
Schools, teachers, and teacher-training bodies (NCERT, SCERT, DIET) promote social health by training students in Life Skills.
Key life skills include Empathy (understanding others' feelings), Self-awareness, Effective Communication, Interpersonal Relationships, Problem-solving, Decision-making, Creative/Critical Thinking, and Coping with Stress and Emotions.
Schools also support social health through healthy canteen food, safe drinking water, and regular health check-ups.
Health includes physical, mental, emotional, and social well-being.
A socially healthy person listens to others, says sorry when wrong, and treats everyone with equality.
Constitutional values—Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity—shape a caring community.
Empathy means putting yourself in another person's shoes to understand their feelings.
Self-awareness means knowing your strengths, beliefs, values, and areas for growth.
Effective communication and problem-solving help students stay stress-free and build strong friendships.

problem.en: Two classmates disagree on a project idea and one starts shouting. Which life skills can resolve this calmly?

text.en: Use coping with emotions and empathy to pause and understand the other's viewpoint.
Use effective communication and problem-solving to combine the best parts of both ideas.

prompt.en: Define social health and explain any three life skills from Chapter 12.

requiredIdeas.en: Social health is positive, harmonious interaction with others
Empathy understands others' feelings; self-awareness recognises one's own strengths and growth areas
Effective communication, problem-solving, and coping with stress build healthy relationships

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking social health just means having many followers online rather than real empathy and respect

points.en: Social health is essential to complete well-being alongside physical and mental health.
Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity guide respectful social living.
Life skills include empathy, self-awareness, communication, problem-solving, and stress coping.
Schools, teachers, and families nurture social health through life-skills training and healthy environments.
